title: Ordered coordinates of a usual module Cech presentation
statement: Let $X,T$ be schemes, $f:X\to T$ a morphism, $M$ a module sheaf on $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $W_i$, $i\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)$, a finite family of opens. Let $D$ be a nonnegative cochain complex of module sheaves whose terms are naturally identified, after restricting scalars to the global ring, by $e_p$ with the usual all-tuple Cech presheaves. For an increasing tuple $t:\operatorname{Fin}(p+1)\hookrightarrow_o\operatorname{Fin}(r)$, put $V_t=\bigcap_lW_{t(l)}$ [def-sc-alternating-cech-total-complex]. Define $j_{t,C}:V_t\cap C\to(\prod_lW_{t(l)})\times C$ by the product lift of the inclusions to each $W_{t(l)}$ and to $C$. Define $q_{p,B,t}$ on the degree-$p$ sections of $L=(f_*D)^{\mathrm{ext}}$ by the extension isomorphism $L^p\cong f_*D^p$, the component of $e_p$ at $f^{-1}B$, the product projection at $t$, and restriction along $j_{t,f^{-1}B}$. It has codomain $\Gamma(V_t\cap f^{-1}B,M)$. The transport $j$ is invertible. The coordinate maps preserve addition and zero, are natural in $B$, and preserve the pulled-back local scalar action when each coordinate of $e$ preserves local scalars.

source.place: Tags 01FJ and 01FK; Coherence part (a), identifying chosen Cech product opens with finite intersections and restricting to increasing tuples

proof.text: Construct the intersection-to-product arrow with prod.lift and Pi.lift. Its projections give the reverse containment, so PartialOrder.isIso_iff_eq proves it is invertible. Define the coordinate by the extension isomorphism, e, the chosen tuple projection, and restriction along this arrow. All maps are actual categorical constructions.

Additivity and preservation of zero follow from map_add and map_zero for each factor. For scalar compatibility use Hom.app_smul on the extension isomorphism, the given local scalar equation for the tuple projection, and map_smul for restriction; map_comp and uniqueness of arrows of opens identify the scalar restriction. For naturality use the extension isomorphism and tuple projection naturality equations, then map_comp and uniqueness of arrows of opens. These are the five proved properties in OrderedCechModuleCoordinates.

proof_origin.note: Explicit coordinate construction and completed Lean proofs of product transport, additivity, zero, scalar compatibility and naturality; proof metadata completed at second reading.

def orderedCechModuleCoordinate {X T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ T)
    (M : X.Modules) {r : ℕ} (W : ULift.{u} (Fin r) → X.Opens)
    (D : CochainComplex X.Modules ℕ)
    (e : ∀ p : ℕ, (PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤)
      isTerminalTop.op).obj (D.X p).val ≅
      ((cechComplexFunctor W).obj
        ((prod.functor (C := X.Opens)).op ⋙ Functor.opHom _ _ ⋙
          (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj M.presheafModuleCat)).X p)
    (p : ℕ) (B : T.Opens) (t : Fin (p + 1) ↪o Fin r)
    (s : Γ(((((Modules.pushforward f).mapHomologicalComplex _).obj D).extend
      ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat).X (p : ℤ), B)) :
    Γ(M, alternatingCechIntersection (fun i ↦ W ⟨i⟩) t ⊓ f ⁻¹ᵁ B)
